text:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xx and TCP timeouts for inference-redwood-usw2 (us-west-2) — elevated error-rate concentrated in az1a. auto-pager sent to oncall-jordan :rotating_light:

oncall-jordan: acked. hopping on bridge now. what’s the impact? which customers?

support-lina: several premium Dedicated customers reporting ~30% request failures, latency up to 8s, some streaming drops. tickets rolling in.

net-ops-sam: looking at VPC flow logs — I see increased retransmits from instances in az1a to NATs, and resolver queries from az1a are timing out intermittently.

sre-maya: I’m seeing repeated ENI detach/attach errors in az1a on G5 fleet nodes, and NLB target health shows a bunch of targets flapping to unhealthy in the same AZ.

eng-ryan: can we confirm it's network plane not model runtime? logs show `socket_econnreset` and `kvcache stall` but CPU/GPU and mem look fine.

net-ops-sam: yeah, kernel rx-drop counters jumping on the hosts. also upstream resolver round-trip is high — `dig +trace` from a healthy node vs an az1a node shows ~250ms vs 20ms.

oncall-jordan: plan: (1) divert traffic away from az1a for public inference routes, (2) drain az1a targets, (3) scale up capacity in az1b/c to absorb, (4) monitor customer errors and notify support. any objections?

sre-maya: agree. start with steering, keep canary at 5% to verify no regressions.

infra-bot: deploy action triggered: set traffic-weight az1a=0 -> az1b=50 az1c=50 via traffic-router API.

eng-ryan: rolling the traffic shift now. adding health-check override to speed exit of unhealthy targets. command:
```
# traffic-router CLI
traffic-router set-weights --region usw2 --weights az1a=0,az1b=60,az1c=40 --canary 5
```

net-ops-sam: while that runs, I recommend editing local resolver config on control-plane proxies to use fallback public resolver to avoid the slowpath. quick change: `/etc/resolv.conf` reorder to `8.8.8.8` first, then local.

sre-maya: making a temporary change to kube-proxy config for L7 health probes to increase retries to avoid flapping during DNS hiccups.

support-lina: prepping customer comms: initial message: "We're seeing elevated errors for inference in us-west-2, mitigation in progress. We'll update in 30m." should we include suggested workaround?

oncall-jordan: yes include that we recommend retrying and enabling client-side exponential backoff for now.

incident-bot: notice: traffic-router change completed. canary at 5% -> no immediate regression.

eng-ryan: canary looks ok. ramping to 50% now.

infra-bot: traffic weights updated: az1a=0, az1b=65, az1c=35.

net-ops-sam: we still see some residual egress jitter originating from az1a instances even though traffic is drained — likely delayed packets in NAT or overloaded NIC TX queues. I'm going to put hosts in az1a into maintenance and trigger instance replacement.

sre-maya: `kubectl drain` commands queued. sample:
```
kubectl drain inference-az1a-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```

eng-ryan: swapping model fallback for a tiny subset of traffic — route to quantized variant `redwood-v0.9-q4` for non-critical customers to reduce memory pressure while we replace nodes.

support-lina: updated broadcast to customers with ETA: initial mitigation in place, full restore depends on AWS host replacements. next update in 20m.

oncall-jordan: handing off to night oncall at 00:30 UTC once replacements progress. leaving bridge open for followups.

net-ops-sam: AWS reports partial host network degradation in az1a — we have open ticket with them, they’re replacing suspect hardware.

eng-ryan: logs from a drained node (snippet):
```
[2026-03-14T22:04:12Z] inference[pid=1245] WARN socket_econnreset remote=10.12.8.45
[2026-03-14T22:04:13Z] inference[pid=1245] ERROR kv_cache_stall key=ctx-7 len=5120
```

incident-bot: incident created: INC-20260314-az1a-net-slowpath. severity: high. commander: oncall-jordan.

support-lina: customers on dedicated reserved pools will be prioritized for traffic into healthy AZs — updated routing policy enforcer.

net-ops-sam: after host replacement started, NIC stats show RX drops returning to baseline. AWS confirmed replacement of a faulty top-of-rack fiber module.

sre-maya: good, start bringing replaced instances back into service slowly and monitor 5xx rate.

infra-bot: re-registering targets in NLB for az1a with gradual ramp (5% increments).

eng-ryan: reintroducing a small portion of capacity in az1a to test stability. if 5xx stays <1% for 10m we can resume normal weights.

incident-bot: update: 5xx rate trending down across region; latency normalized for most customers.

support-lina: sending customers a post-incident note offering timeline and mitigation steps; recording RCA request.

oncall-jordan: handing off to night shift (oncall-kim). we're in monitoring state. please ping if anything spikes. :white_check_mark: 

oncall-kim: acked, monitoring. setting follow-up ticket for full RCA and improvements (resolver fallback, NLB health tuning, cross-AZ pre-warm).

sre-maya: notes for RCA: add better telemetry on per-AZ resolver RTT, automatic traffic-shed thresholds, and tighter NLB deregistration grace.

support-lina: closing thread to reduce noise for customers; will reopen if regressions. final status in 2 hours or on RCA publication. :email:
